issues.body: `repair_lane_owned` still returns true for a `dirty` same-repository pull without validating `pull.head.sha`. Both `stale_worker_pr_reason` and `age_park_cause_recovered` therefore treat that pull as repair-lane-owned, but `enumerate_review_items` rejects a missing, non-string, short, or non-hex SHA at its unconditional `SAFE_SHA.fullmatch(sha)` gate before reaching `needs-rebase`. This can suppress the visible age park or spend the one-shot re-admission grant while dispatch emits nothing indefinitely. `_rl_pull` always supplies `_rl_sha`; the stale-status test supplies another valid 40-hex SHA and tests snapshot mismatch, not malformed live-head rejection. Thus the prior-round hole remains untested and unfixed.
issues.fix_hint: Make the shared ownership predicate require the same well-formed live head SHA required by dispatch, failing closed when it is absent or malformed. Add paired park-entry and park-exit tests for missing, non-string, short, and non-hex `head.sha`, and pass those identical pull shapes through the real enumerator to prove it emits no item while groom keeps the visible park. Retain a valid 40-hex same-repository positive control proving both exemption and re-admission still deliver `needs-rebase`.
issues.title: Repair ownership still omits dispatch's terminal head-SHA gate

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 5 leaves the prior major delivery gap unchanged. `repair_lane_owned` still proves only the `dirty` merge state and exact same-repository head repository; it does not validate the live `head.sha`. The real dispatch enumerator unconditionally rejects a missing or malformed SHA before it can emit `needs-rebase`. Consequently groom can still suppress a visible age park or consume the bounded standing-park re-admission grant for a pull that dispatch will never enumerate. The delivery fixture continues to hard-code a valid 40-hex SHA, and the stale-snapshot row uses another valid SHA, so neither exercises the malformed live-head gate. The same major finding remains at the same severity, so progress is stagnant.
